title: Deployment escort: stepwise traffic throttles and adaptive rollback thresholds
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current rollout tooling uses static % ramps and single-threshold rollbacks which do not adapt to heterogeneous traffic profiles (short chat requests vs long-context completions), LTS channel requirements, or partial infra degradation. This leads to noisy rollbacks and manual interventions for multi-region and model-variant deployments.\n\nGoal: Build a "deployment escort" system that manages staged progressive delivery with stepwise traffic throttles, cohort-aware ramp curves, hysteresis to avoid oscillation, feature-flag escorting (ensuring feature flags are toggled with traffic windows), and adaptive rollback thresholds that factor in baseline drift, cohort weight, and rolling-history anomalies. The escort should integrate with Console rollouts, Dedicated autoscaling signals, and Private deployment upgrade plans.
acceptance_criteria: New rollout policy type 'deployment-escort' available in Console and infra API
Traffic ramps can be defined as piecewise step curves per-cohort (eg: 0->1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50%) with per-step hold windows
Adaptive rollback decisions use configurable windowed baselines and provide graded remediation (attenuate traffic, pause, rollback, open circuit)
Feature flags can be bound to escort policies so a flag toggle is applied only when a cohort reaches a defined traffic weight
Canary cohorts support region/model-specific thresholds and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant on capacity shortfall
End-to-end e2e test harness demonstrating canary rollout for a model change with a simulated latency/regression and automated attenuation -> rollback flow
Runbook generated and linked; on-call can trigger manual override and see telemetry-driven rationale for auto-actions
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal canary (team-only) 1% -> 5% hold 30m -> 20% hold 60m. Phase B: Cross-region 5% -> 25% hold 60m -> 50% hold 2h. Phase C: Ramp to target (LTS vs edge non-LTS) with per-channel max cap. Each step evaluates SLOs and anomaly score; on anomaly>threshold run graded remediation. Feature flags bound to cohorts only enabled after a cohort passes the "stability gate" (no severe anomalies in last N minutes).
migration_steps: 1) Add 'deployment-escort' policy schema and validation. 2) Implement escort controller that consumes metrics and makes step decisions. 3) Wire controller to traffic router and feature-flag service. 4) Add canary simulation harness and chaos tests. 5) Create Console UI for configuring escort policies. 6) Pilot on non-prod then prod with low-risk model change.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Aggressive attenuation preserves availability but delays exposure to full capacity which can increase rollout time for critical fixes.
Decision: Use hysteresis windows and a two-tier anomaly score (service-level and customer-visible errors) to reduce false positives.
Choice: Start with telemetry-backed decisions; add ML-based anomaly predictions in a later iteration to avoid operational complexity now.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial proposal created after incident INC-2026-02-19 where static rollback caused oscillation during a multi-region model upgrade.

2026-02-26 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete; prototype controller is routing simulated traffic and applying step changes locally. Observed that short-lived spikes on p99 cause unnecessary rollbacks; adding median-trim windows.
2026-03-03 - PM review (Sophie Martinez): Requested explicit support for LTS vs non-LTS channels and ability to set different max caps per channel. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Daniel Kim): Console UX mockups uploaded to Confluence; suggested an 'escort summary' card showing current step, health, and recent actions.

2026-03-08 - Engineering note: Implemented graded remediation actions: attenuate (reduce by x%), pause (stop progression), open-circuit (rollback to previous stable) and emergency rollback. Unit and integration tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289
2026-03-10 - Security (Alyssa Tran): Quick review completed; feature-flag binding requires RBAC check which will be enforced by the controller. No blockers.
